sections.title: Control Is Software Now.
sections.body: NavierOS — flight control and autonomy — flies the foils hundreds of times per second. The result is a vessel that is foilborne-stable through Sea State 4 — pitch and roll held to under 1°, flight height held to ±2 cm, electric-quiet on station, and software-defined: the same control platform runs every hull in the family.

sections.title: Unmanned Today. Autonomous by Stages.
sections.body: The craft that ran at SOCOM TE 26-3 was unmanned — commanded over a hardened datalink with defined loss-of-link behaviors, from the helm or a ground control station. Autonomy is layered onto that same control core in stages — each one demonstrated on the water.

rungs.label: Flight control
rungs.body: NavierOS flies the foils hundreds of times a second — 10,000+ operating hours. Stable through Sea State 4; every autonomy layer inherits it.

rungs.label: Unmanned operation
rungs.body: Helm and ground-control-station commanding · dual-antenna GNSS + inertial navigation · Starlink and hardened datalink with defined loss-of-link behaviors. Run live at SOCOM TE 26-3, August 2026.

rungs.label: Perception
rungs.body: Vision-first, sensor-fused. Live scene segmentation, stereo depth and 3D harbor mapping from real operations; radar and AIS fusion being added. 74,000+ images captured in one week of demonstrations.

rungs.label: Vehicle autonomy
rungs.body: Heading hold, waypoint following and station-keeping in simulation; on-water N30 trials — Q4 2026, first milestone filmed by December. Advisory detect-and-avoid rides beside the operator on every trial — every trial adds to the autonomy record.

sections.fleet_data_line: Every hull logs perception, telemetry and energy data to a central fleet database. Every hour the commercial fleet flies hardens the same stack the defense fleet runs.

media.caption: What the boat sees — raw camera feeds (left) and live scene segmentation: sky, land, water, vessel, people (right). N30 operations, Idaho, August 2026.
Stereo depth on a dock approach — left camera, point cloud, depth map. Pilings, dock edge and hulls resolved in 3D from a bow-mounted stereo camera. Sausalito, August 2026.
The boat maps its own harbor — shoreline and docks reconstructed in 3D from the run itself, track overlaid. Alameda estuary, August 2026.
Waypoint following and heading hold in simulation, commanded from the NavierOS helm display — the same screen the operator uses on the water.
